observation: Round 1 (binary 127->110, oblique/horizontal Hough 30->25, maxLineGap_oblique 30->45, K_height 840) moved the proxy the wrong way: 0.641 -> 0.621, driven entirely by correspondence_f1@15 falling 0.364 -> 0.326 while sam_fill_rate (0.729 -> 0.728), ring_count_error (0) and depth_nan_ratio (0.131) were unchanged. The round-1 detected_lines.png explains the drop: the two long K-edge obliques (green ~y1450-1480 to x~1600, red ~y1620-1640 to x~1900) are now continuous, but the relaxed accumulator also admitted a cloud of 40-60 px fragments in the dense bolt-pattern region x~60-350 (y~1350-1750, ~1930, ~2400) plus short horizontal stubs at y~780/2300 that sit >15 px from the SAM A/B boundaries. Those extra lines are unexplained by any label boundary, so F1 precision fell faster than recall rose. The long A/B joints at y~785 and ~2300 remain undetectable as long lines because horizontal minLineLength/maxLineGap are fixed priors, so recall on those rows is not a lever available in this space. Stages 1-3 remain healthy (residual 2.8 cm, orient corr 0.999, retention 0.77) and all 10 prompts still snap to the K row (y~1553; det_fallback_ratio 1.0 is the expected snap regime). Ring pitch from the synthetic verticals is ~245 px = 1225 mm versus segment_width 1200 mm (240 px), i.e. SAM ring crops are ~5 px narrower than the ring spacing.
rule: Ontology d9/f_spurious_lines with remediation r_tighten_hough (raise oblique threshold; the precondition f_under_gate is ruled out because retention and NaN are unchanged and the fragments come from real bolt-hole texture, not background leakage). Experiences sec.5: more detected lines is not better - consistency with the structure is what matters; sec.9: use the proxy delta directionally and reverse a move that degraded coherence. Ontology r_fix_template: segment geometry (segment_width) should match the measured ring pitch so per-ring crops tile the map without gaps; experiences sec.8 (t3): trust the round-to-round proxy delta.
failure_mode: stage_4_detection.f_spurious_lines (round-1 Hough relaxation produced unexplained short fragments that lowered correspondence precision) with a residual mild stage_5_segmentation.f_template_mismatch (ring crop width 240 px vs measured 245 px pitch).
rationale: Reverse the round-1 direction and tighten detection so only the long, boundary-consistent K-edge lines survive: binary_threshold 110->135 (slightly above the 127 default) so faint bolt-hole pixels drop out of the binarised outlier map before dilation; hough_threshold_oblique 25->40 so 40-60 px fragments no longer reach the accumulator while the multi-hundred-px K-edge obliques keep their votes; hough_threshold_horizontal 25->35 to prune the isolated horizontal stubs that were mostly orange; maxLineGap_oblique 45->40 (kept above the 30 prior) so the K-edge lines remain continuous rather than splitting back into fragments. Vertical accumulator and uniform_k_snap untouched to keep the 10 synthetic verticals and K-row gating identical. SAM: K_height back to the 823.8 mm T3 prior (the 840 nudge produced no measurable fill/F1 change; the SAM K boundary follows the depth discontinuity, not the template height), angle stays 6.12, and segment_width 1200->1225 mm to match the measured 245 px ring pitch so adjacent ring crops tile without the ~5 px gap. Denoising and enhancing untouched (experiences sec.4/7). Expected: fewer orange (unexplained) lines, unchanged cyan coverage on the K edges -> correspondence F1 back above the anchor 0.364; fill rate flat or slightly up; NaN and ring count unchanged.
